title: intermittent-401-429-play-by-play
content:
Quick notes / running log for the intermittent 401/429 bursts we saw against hosted API keys. This is a personal scratchpad — not polished.

Summary:
- Impact: intermittent 401 and 429 errors from multiple customers between 2026-02-19 03:40 UTC and 2026-02-19 05:10 UTC. Mostly short bursts (~2–5 min) but recurring across a few keys.
- Symptoms: clients receive either HTTP 401 (Unauthorized) or HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests). 401s are not correlated 1:1 with token expiry; some keys that were valid seconds earlier suddenly 401. 429s include X-RateLimit headers in ~30% of responses, but many 429s lacked header info (suggests proxy or gateway rate-limit).
- Suspected causes (working hypotheses): API key rotation job overlapping active keys, edge proxy misrouting/returning stale auth cache, quota enforcement bug at rate-limiter that double-counts batched requests, or a background job generating short burst of requests under the same key.

Timeline + notable observations: (UTC)
- 2026-02-19 03:38 — Pager alerts start, SRE channel shows initial 401s from customer A.
- 03:40 — Observed first group of 401s in ingress logs for key K_a. Token lookup shows key still present in DB (last rotated 2026-01-12).
- 03:42 — 429s begin for different key K_b from same customer environment; upstream shows burst of 1.2k rps for ~15s.
- 03:45 — 401s and 429s interleave; some clients get 401 then immediately retry and receive 429.
- 03:55 — Mitigation: throttling rule relaxed for the route for 10m, some reduction but still occasional 401s.
- 04:10 — Rotated API key for customer A proactively (issued new key), customers report resumed success for that key.
- 04:20 — Pattern repeats for other customers (C, D).
- 05:00 — Root cause not confirmed; opened INFR-4231.

Commands / checks I ran (local env):
- Check key state in auth DB:
  psql -h auth-db.internal -U readonly -c "select id, active, rotated_at, last_used_at from api_keys where id='K_a'"
  -> shows active=true, rotated_at=2026-01-12, last_used_a ~ 2026-02-19 03:39:58

- Inspect ingress logs (kinesis tail):
  aws logs tail /prod/ingress --start-time 2026-02-19T03:30:00Z --filter-pattern "status=401 OR status=429"
  -> snippets: multiple 401s with response_reason="invalid-credentials" and 429s with response_reason="rate-limited"

- Example 401 snippet (raw):
  {
    "ts": "2026-02-19T03:40:12.123Z",
    "req_id": "req-abc123",
    "status": 401,
    "reason": "invalid-credentials",
    "api_key_id": "K_a"
  }

- Example 429 snippet (raw):
  {
    "ts": "2026-02-19T03:42:05.789Z",
    "req_id": "req-def456",
    "status": 429,
    "reason": "rate-limited",
    "api_key_id": "K_b",
    "headers": {
      "x-ratelimit-limit": "120",
      "x-ratelimit-remaining": "0"
    }
  }

- Crosschecked token introspection service (introspect logs):
  curl -s -X POST https://introspect.internal/api -d "key=K_a" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -> responded: active=true, exp=1700000000, last_used=2026-02-19T03:39:58Z

- Edge cache logs (envoy/xds): looked for cache invalidations around 03:38–03:44. Found a periodic job (api-key-sync) that runs every 5 minutes and does a bulk TTL refresh. Job run at 03:40:00 with duration 6s.

Error patterns and oddities:
- 401s are concentrated within seconds after api-key-sync run in some pods.
- Some 429s appeared without X-RateLimit headers; likely generated by upstream CDN/gateway rather than app.
- When a client switched to the new rotated key (issued at 04:10), they stopped getting 401s but other keys on same account continued to see 429s.
- In a couple of cases clients reported deterministic 401 after a ~300ms retry window (client retried quickly and got 401).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Edge/proxy cache invalidation race: api-key-sync clears or refreshes in-memory auth cache, and some proxy pods temporarily treat keys as missing (401) during the refresh window. Evidence: 401 spike aligns with api-key-sync run; errors concentrated on small subset of pods that logged cache miss.
2) Key rotation scheduler: a background rotation attempt flagged keys temporarily unverified for a few seconds. Less likely since rotated_at for K_a is older and we issued new key at 04:10 which fixed the issue for that client (could be masking the real cause).
3) Rate-limiter misconfiguration: quota engine double-counts when requests are proxied through internal batching layer. Explains 429s and missing headers if the gateway triggers early before application sees it.
4) Upstream proxy (CDN) overloaded and returning 401/429 incorrectly under heavy connection churn.

Quick experiments to reproduce locally:
- Re-run api-key-sync locally against a test cluster while generating a low-rate stream of requests for key K_test. Observe if 401s spike on pods with sync activity.
- Simulate concurrent requests that arrive while auth cache is being updated (spawn 500 parallel requests with slight offsets).
- Use tcpdump/strace on a pod to see if auth validation call to introspect service returns 200 but pod still returns 401 (would show internal logic bug).

Notes from pods that flashed 401 (pod logs):
- Pod: frontend-rt-5
  03:40:00.123 INFO Started api-key-sync run (batch=1000)
  03:40:00.456 WARN auth-cache: key K_a not found in local cache
  03:40:01.000 ERROR auth: token validation failed (introspect ok) -> returning 401

- Pod: frontend-rt-7 (didn't run sync)
  03:40:03 INFO request req-xyz processed status=200

This supports hypothesis 1 (race/mis-synced cache).

Mitigations applied so far:
- Short-term: staggered api-key-sync runs across pods (patched schedule to randomize start times) — pushed 2026-02-19 06:00 UTC.
- Short-term: added extra logging around auth cache misses and added metric auth.cache_miss_count by pod.
- Customer mitigation: rotated keys for a few impacted customers to stop immediate 401s (manual).

Next steps / TODOs: (owner = Priya)
- [ ] Reproduce locally with controlled sync + requests (priority: high).
- [ ] Add a canary that forces a sync on a single non-prod pod and run traffic to measure failure window (priority: high).
- [ ] Add distributed lock or CAS semantics to api-key-sync so cache entries are replaced atomically (eng infra task).
- [ ] Instrument the gateway to always propagate X-RateLimit headers when returning 429 so we can triage source of rate-limits.
- [ ] Confirm whether quota double-counting is happening for requests that traverse batching layer (ask eng-serving-runtime to review counter implementation).
- [ ] Add automated alerts when auth.cache_miss_count spikes > threshold.

Random notes / ideas:
- Could we use a TTL-on-write approach instead of full bulk refresh? Smaller deltas reduce the window for inconsistency.
- Consider adding ephemeral per-pod fallback to call introspect synchronously if cache miss occurs (to avoid returning 401). Might be slightly higher latency but safer.
- If gateway is swallowing headers, add a tracer id in header to follow request through layers.

Open questions:
- Why do some 429s lack headers? (gateway vs application)
- Are retries from SDKs exacerbating bursts? Check client-side retry config.
- Is there any scheduled job at 03:40 in customers' envs that aligns with bursts? (customer said no, but we should check their telemetry)

Attachments / references:
- INFR-4231 incident ticket (root doc)
- Slack thread #infra-auth-incident (thread-ck9f2)
- Local scripts used to simulate: scripts/simulate_sync_race.sh (internal repo)

If anyone else is debugging, add notes here. Will update after running local reproducer and patch landing.

-- Priya
